title: Why ASML Is Racing to Build 110 EUV Machines - Semiwiki
gist: ASML is exploring producing more than 110 EUV lithography machines in 2028 (up ~30% from an already-planned 80+ in 2027), driven by AI-infrastructure demand for leading-edge logic and high-bandwidth memory; the bottleneck is assembly throughput rather than supplier shortages, per JPMorgan, positioning ASML as a critical chokepoint/beneficiary of the AI capex boom.

insights.claim: ASML is exploring production of more than 110 EUV lithography machines in 2028, an increase of roughly 30% versus the at-least-80 systems it expects to manufacture in 2027; the 2028 figure is a capacity scenario, not yet a firm production commitment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A leading capacity signal for the entire leading-edge semiconductor supply chain; investors should track whether ASML converts this scenario into firm 2028 orders as a bellwether for sustained AI capex.
insights.quote: ASML is exploring how to produce more than 110 extreme ultraviolet lithography machines in 2028

insights.claim: ASML is the only company commercially supplying EUV lithography systems at scale, making its production capacity a critical constraint on how rapidly the global semiconductor industry can expand leading-edge manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: ASML's monopoly position in EUV makes it a structural chokepoint/moat play for the entire AI hardware buildout — a key reason to treat ASML capacity announcements as leading indicators for foundry/memory capacity growth broadly.
insights.quote: ASML is the only company commercially supplying EUV lithography systems at scale, making its production capacity a critical constraint on how rapidly the semiconductor industry can expand leading-edge manufacturing.

insights.claim: ASML was already nearly fully booked for 2027 according to a Reuters report, with many newer orders intended for delivery in 2028.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Near-full 2027 bookings indicate durable, multi-year demand visibility for ASML rather than a short-term spike, supporting a longer investment horizon thesis for lithography capex.
insights.quote: ASML was already nearly fully booked for 2027, with many newer orders intended for delivery in 2028.

insights.claim: JPMorgan analysts identified the principal limitation on ASML's output as the speed at which it can assemble EUV systems, rather than shortages across its supplier network — a distinction that matters because improving internal assembly throughput is more manageable than rebuilding an entire supply chain.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: If the bottleneck is internal assembly capacity (solvable via investment/hiring/process improvement) rather than external supplier scarcity, ASML's capacity ramp is more credible and de-risked than if it depended on third parties.
insights.quote: JPMorgan analysts said the principal limitation was the speed at which ASML could assemble EUV systems rather than shortages throughout its supplier network.

insights.claim: The immediate driver of ASML's expansion plan is AI: companies building AI infrastructure need advanced accelerators, which depend on leading-edge foundry capacity and high-bandwidth memory, both of which require increasingly intensive use of lithography.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Confirms the AI capex cycle is propagating upstream into equipment capital goods, not just chip design and data-center buildout — a useful cross-check for the durability of the broader AI infrastructure trade.
insights.quote: The immediate driver is AI. Training and operating increasingly capable AI models requires enormous quantities of computing power.

insights.claim: ASML has said its logic business is benefiting from foundries adding capacity for new process nodes, while demand for high-bandwidth memory and DDR5 is supporting growth in its memory business.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Both ASML's logic and memory segments are seeing AI-driven tailwinds simultaneously, broadening the demand base beyond just leading-edge logic (e.g., Nvidia-adjacent) to memory suppliers like SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung.
insights.quote: ASML has said its logic business is benefiting from foundries adding capacity for new process nodes, while demand for high-bandwidth memory and DDR5 is supporting growth in its memory business.

insights.claim: As semiconductor manufacturers move to smaller process geometries, they generally use EUV on more layers per chip, meaning demand for ASML systems can rise faster than the number of wafers being produced.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A structural multiplier effect: node shrinkage alone (independent of wafer volume growth) increases EUV tool demand, supporting a durable long-term growth thesis for ASML even if wafer starts plateau.
insights.quote: Consequently, demand for ASML systems can rise faster than the number of wafers being produced.

insights.claim: ASML is introducing High-NA EUV, a next-generation technology capable of printing smaller features, with wider adoption expected to begin around 2028 and develop more significantly over the following decade.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: High-NA EUV adoption timing (2028 inflection, scaling through the 2030s) is a multi-year revenue driver layered on top of the current EUV ramp — worth tracking as a distinct ASML growth vector.
insights.quote: Wider High-NA adoption is expected to begin around 2028 and develop more significantly during the following decade, adding another dimension to the company's expansion.

insights.claim: Additional EUV machine availability could support faster construction and ramp-up of advanced fabrication capacity at TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix and Micron, though more machines alone do not instantly translate into more chips since factories also need buildings, utilities, other process equipment, trained personnel and sufficient yields.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Investors should not assume ASML capacity expansion alone resolves AI-chip supply bottlenecks; other capacity inputs (fab construction, workforce, yield) remain binding constraints even with more EUV tools available.
insights.quote: More machines do not instantly translate into more chips—factories also need buildings, utilities, process equipment, trained personnel, and sufficient yields—but lithography is among the most important pieces of the capacity equation.

insights.claim: Key risks to ASML's expansion plan include AI infrastructure spending slowing if customers fail to earn adequate returns on capital investments, the historically cyclical nature of semiconductor demand turning excess boom-era capacity into a liability, export restrictions (particularly affecting China sales), and the challenge of maintaining quality while raising output of an extraordinarily complex precision machine.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A concise risk checklist for the ASML/AI-capex bull thesis: watch AI infrastructure ROI trends, semiconductor cycle indicators, and China export-control developments as key downside triggers.
insights.quote: AI infrastructure spending could slow if customers struggle to earn adequate returns from their enormous capital investments.

insights.claim: ASML is preparing production capacity before holding purchase orders for every potential 2028 system, because customer forecasts are already strong enough to justify early action.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: ASML investing ahead of firm orders signals high management confidence in AI-driven demand durability — a bullish forward signal worth weighing against cyclicality risk.
insights.quote: ASML is preparing before it holds purchase orders for every potential 2028 system because customer forecasts are strong enough to justify early action.
